definitions.Tugzh-el: Named after the ancient Ruskalan word 'tugzh,' meaning 'iron,' and 'el,' meaning 'river' — literally 'Iron River,' the name of a man said to have lived along the frozen waterway where iron ore was first smelted in the northern provinces.
definitions.Shazga-sikhd: Built from 'shazga,' meaning 'hawk,' and 'sikhd,' meaning 'stone-cutter' — a surname meaning 'hawk stone-cutter,' traditionally given to families of skilled masons who carved the great granite monuments of old Ruskalan.
definitions.Mzyrthe-marsh: Derived from 'mzyr,' meaning 'marshland,' and 'the,' an archaic possessive particle — a name meaning 'of the marsh,' originally given to those born or raised in the boggy lowlands south of the Greylake region.
definitions.Zugsh-or: Composed of 'zugsh,' meaning 'gray,' and 'or,' meaning 'mountain' — literally 'Gray Mountain,' a name given to settlers who were among the first to build homes on the slopes of Mount Ashkara, whose peaks are perpetually shrouded in mist.
definitions.Rromga-thigf: From 'rromga,' meaning 'journey' or 'road,' and 'thigf,' meaning 'keeper' or 'warden' — a name meaning 'road keeper,' traditionally held by families responsible for maintaining the old trade routes through the mountain passes.
definitions.Chizf-im: Built from 'chizf,' meaning 'sharp' or 'keen,' and 'im,' an honorific particle meaning 'the one who' — a name meaning 'the one who is sharp,' given to warriors or strategists renowned for their cunning and precision in battle.
definitions.Lochsh-or: Derived from 'lochsh,' meaning 'silence' or 'stillness,' and 'or,' meaning 'mountain' — literally 'Silence Mountain,' a name given to a hermit who withdrew to live alone on a remote peak and was said to never speak a word for ten years.
definitions.Folsh-or: From 'folsh,' meaning 'deep' or 'profound,' and 'or,' meaning 'mountain' — literally 'Deep Mountain,' a name given to miners who ventured into the deepest caverns beneath Mount Kordal, where the tunnels were said to reach the bones of the earth.
definitions.Thazzh-um: Composed of 'thazzh,' meaning 'wrath' or 'fury,' and 'um,' meaning 'son' or 'child' — a name meaning 'son of fury,' given to a warrior born during a great battle and believed to carry the spirit of vengeance from his mother's side.
definitions.Sh-odga-jant: Built from 'sh,' meaning 'the,' 'odga,' meaning 'sword,' and 'jant,' meaning 'bearer' or 'carrier' — a name meaning 'the sword-bearer,' an honorific title given to the chief knight or champion of a Ruskalan lord, passed down through generations.
